J." Figueroa Mercado''' (born March 28, 1998) is a Dominican and American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Mexico City Capitanes]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Odessa College|Odessa Wranglers]], the [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's Red Storm]], and the [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon Ducks]]. ==High school career== As a freshman, Figueroa played basketball for [[Notre Dame Cristo Rey High School]] in [[Lawrence, Massachusetts]]. For his sophomore season, he transferred to [[Lawrence High School (Massachusetts)|Lawrence High School]] in Lawrence to seek better competition but was relegated to [[junior varsity team|junior varsity]]. He then transferred to Oldsmar Christian School in [[Oldsmar, Florida]], where he repeated his sophomore year and grew four inches (10 cm).{{cite web |last1=Muldoon |first1=Michael |title=L.J. Figueroa: From Lawrence benchwarmer to Florida All-American |url=https://www.eagletribune.com/sports/l-j-figueroa-from-lawrence-benchwarmer-to-florida-all-american/article_fa0c28e4-e738-5de6-a847-89ddf070acbc.html |website=[[The Eagle-Tribune]] |accessdate=October 27, 2020 |date=August 16, 2015}} Figueroa was drawn there by coach Alex Arias.{{cite web |last1=Braziller |first1=Zach |title='I wanted more for myself': St. John's star's leap of faith pays off |url=https://nypost.com/2019/03/19/i-wanted-more-for-myself-st-johns-stars-leap-of-faith-pays-off/ |website=[[New York Post]] |accessdate=October 27, 2020 |date=March 19, 2019}} For his senior season, he moved to West Oaks Academy in [[Orlando, Florida]].{{cite web |last1=Bensley |first1=Alex |title=Lawrence's LJ Figueroa emerging as a shooting star at St. John's University |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/sports/high-schools/2019/02/21/lawrence-figueroa-emerging-shooting-star-john-university/a6jFB5pSO2Tr3z9PuiyH8K/story.html |website=[[The Boston Globe]] |accessdate=October 27, 2020 |date=February 21, 2019}} Figueroa was a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and committed to play college basketball for [[New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball|New Mexico State]] over offers from [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]], [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami (Florida)]] and [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]], among others.{{cite web |last1=Rudi |first1=Mark |title=Top 100 recruit L.J. Figueroa commits to New Mexico State |url=https://www.lcsun-news.com/story/sports/college/blogs/off-the-mark/2016/11/15/nmsu-lands-commitment-top-100-recruit-lj-figueroa/93941452/ |website=[[Las Cruces Sun-News]] |accessdate=October 27, 2020 |date=November 15, 2016}} ==College career== Before playing a game for New Mexico State, Figueroa left the program due to a coaching change. He played for [[Odessa College]] during his freshman season.{{cite web |last1=Sturm |first1=Taylor |title=L.J. Figueroa: Four-star college basketball recruit going JUCO, not New Mexico State |url=https://bustingbrackets.com/2017/05/31/l-j-figueroa-four-star-college-basketball-recruit-going-juco-not-new-mexico-state/ |website=Busting Brackets |accessdate=October 27, 2020 |date=May 31, 2017}} Figueroa averaged 21.4 points, 5.5 rebounds and 3.7 assists per game, while shooting 48.2 percent from three-point range, and earned First Team [[National Junior College Athletic Association]] Division I All-American honors.{{cite web |last1=Muldoon |first1=Michael |title=Under the Lights: L.J. Figueroa the new King of Queens |url=https://www.eagletribune.com/sports/local_sports/under-the-lights-l-j-figueroa-the-new-king-of-queens/article_a3c97286-bf55-5c79-9a22-c59d0a37c396.html |website=[[The Eagle-Tribune]] |accessdate=October 27, 2020 |date=May 13, 2018}}{{cite web |title=St. John's Signs LJ Figueroa |url=https://redstormsports.com/news/2018/4/21/St_John_s_Signs_LJ_Figueroa |website=St. John's University Athletics |accessdate=October 27, 2020 |date=April 21, 2018}} He was also named [[Western Junior College Athletic Conference]] (WJCAC) Player of the Year and Freshman of the Year.{{cite web |title=WJCAC All-Conference Basketball |url=https://njcaaregion5.com/sports/mbkb/2017-18/releases/20180312w6s353 |publisher=NJCAA Region 5 |accessdate=October 27, 2020 |date=March 12, 2018}} For his sophomore season, Figueroa transferred to [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]]. On November 27, 2018, he scored a sophomore season-high 25 points and collected 13 rebounds in an 85–64 win against [[Maryland Eastern Shore Hawks men's basketball|Maryland Eastern Shore]].{{cite news |title=St. John's beats Maryland-Eastern Shore 85–64 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401083340 |accessdate=October 28, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 27, 2018}} As a sophomore, Figueroa averaged 14.4 points, 6.4 rebounds and 1.7 assists per game. He entered the transfer portal following the departure of coach [[Chris Mullin]] before returning to St. John's.{{cite web |last1=Phillips |first1=Scott |title=LJ Figueroa staying at St. John's |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2019/05/15/lj-figueroa-staying-at-st-johns/ |website=[[NBC Sports]] |accessdate=October 27, 2020 |date=May 15, 2019}} On January 25, 2020, Figueroa scored a junior season-high 28 points with seven three-pointers in a 79–66 win over [[DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball|DePaul]].{{cite web |title=Figueroa lifts St. John's over DePaul 79–66 |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2020/01/25/figueroa-lifts-st-johns-over-depaul-79-66/41064667/ |website=[[USA Today]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |accessdate=October 27, 2020 |date=January 25, 2020}} As a junior, he averaged 14.5 points, 4.5 rebounds, 2.1 assists and a [[Big East Conference|Big East]]-leading 1.9 steals per game.{{cite web |last1=Rubin |first1=Roger |title=St. John's Figueroa enters transfer portal |url=https://www.newsday.com/sports/college/st-johns/lj-figueroa-transfer-portal-h66319 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200606193437/https://www.newsday.com/sports/college/st-johns/lj-figueroa-transfer-portal-1.44964128 |url-status=live |archive-date=June 6, 2020 |website=[[Newsday]] |access-date=October 27, 2020 |date=May 26, 2020}} However, Figueroa struggled with his shooting under new coach [[Mike Anderson (basketball, born 1959)|Mike Anderson]], making 37.9 percent of his attempts from the floor.{{cite news |last1=Braziller |first1=Zach |title=The reality of LJ Figueroa's separation from St. John's |url=https://nypost.com/2020/05/27/the-reality-of-lj-figueroas-separation-from-st-johns/ |accessdate=October 28, 2020 |work=[[New York Post]] |date=May 27, 2020}} After initially declaring for the [[2020 NBA draft]], Figueroa decided to return to college and transfer to [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]] for his senior season.{{cite web |title=St. John's wing LJ Figueroa transferring to Oregon |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29342567/st-john-wing-lj-figueroa-transferring-oregon |website=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=October 27, 2020 |date=June 21, 2020}} He was granted a waiver for immediate eligibility on December 3.{{cite news |last1=Crepea |first1=James |title=LJ Figueroa granted eligibility waiver from NCAA, can play for Oregon Ducks against Seton Hall |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/ducks/2020/12/lj-figueroa-granted-eligibility-waiver-from-ncaa-can-play-for-oregon-ducks-against-seton-hall.html |access-date=December 3, 2020 |work=[[The Oregonian]] |date=December 3, 2020}} As a senior, Figueroa averaged 12.3 points and a team-high 6.1 rebounds per game, while finishing third on the team with 41 steals. Following the season, he opted to turn professional rather than take advantage of the additional season of eligibility the NCAA granted due to the COVID-19 pandemic.{{cite news |last1=Hansen |first1=Chris |title=Oregon men's basketball's LJ Figueroa moving on to a pro career |url=https://www.registerguard.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2021/04/20/oregon-ducks-mens-basketballs-lj-figueroa-moving-pro-career/7309768002/ |access-date=September 2, 2021 |work=[[The Register-Guard]] |date=April 20, 2021}} ==Professional career== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Figueroa joined the [[Dallas Mavericks]] for [[NBA Summer League]] play.{{cite news|first1=Jared|last1=Mack|title=Ducks flourish as NBA Summer League comes to an end|url=https://247sports.com/college/oregon/Article/Ducks-flourish-as-Summer-League-comes-to-an-end-Oregon-basketball-Bol-Bol-Summer-League-Louis-King-Payton-Pritchard-Eugene-Omoruyi-169303922/|work=247 Sports|date=August 18, 2021|access-date=September 2, 2021}} ===Leones de Santo Domingo (2021)=== In August, he signed with [[Leones de Santo Domingo]] of the Dominican [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto]],{{cite news|title=L.J. Figueroa debutará este martes con los Leones de Santo Domingo|url=https://listindiario.com/el-deporte/2021/08/30/686065/l-j-figueroa-debutara-este-martes-con-los-leones-de-santo-domingo|work=Listin Diario|date=August 30, 2021|access-date=October 15, 2021|language=Spanish}} helping them win the LNB Championship.{{cite web|title=Los Leones de Santo Domingo se proclamaron campeones de la LNB tras derrotar a los Titanes|url=https://proceso.com.do/2021/10/02/los-leones-de-santo-domingo-se-proclamaron-campeones-de-la-lnb-tras-derrotar-a-los-titanes/|work=Proceso.com.do|date=October 2, 2021|access-date=October 17, 2021|language=Spanish}} ===Santa Cruz Warriors (2021–2022)=== On October 13, 2021, Figueroa signed with the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{cite web|title=Warriors Sign L.J. Figueroa|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-sign-lj-figueroa|website=NBA.com|date=October 13, 2021|access-date=October 14, 2021}} However, he was waived three days later.{{cite web|title=Warriors Waive L.J. Figueroa and Axel Toupane|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-waive-lj-figueroa-and-axel-toupane|website=NBA.com|date=October 16, 2021|access-date=October 17, 2021}} In October 2021, Figueroa joined the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] as an affiliate player.{{cite news |last1=Seimas |first1=Jim |title=Santa Cruz Warriors reveal training camp roster NBA G League |url=https://www.santacruzsentinel.com/2021/10/26/santa-cruz-warriors-reveal-training-camp-roster-nba-g-league/ |access-date=November 1, 2021 |work=[[Santa Cruz Sentinel]] |date=October 26, 2021}} On January 10, 2022, he had 17 points and 13 rebounds and hit the game-winning basket at the buzzer in a 132–130 overtime win over the [[Memphis Hustle]].{{cite news |last1=Seimas |first1=Jim |title=LJ Figueroa's buzzer-beater lifts Santa Cruz in OT |url=https://www.santacruzsentinel.com/2022/01/10/lj-figueroas-buzzer-beater-lifts-santa-cruz-in-ot-nba-g-league/ |access-date=February 6, 2022 |work=[[Santa Cruz Sentinel]] |date=January 10, 2022}} ===South Bay Lakers (2022–2023)=== On October 8, 2022, Figueroa signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|title=Lakers Sign LJ Figueroa and Shaquille Harrison|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/lakers-sign-lj-figueroa-and-shaquille-harrison-100822|website=NBA.com|date=October 8, 2022|access-date=October 8, 2022}} He was waived two days later.{{Cite tweet |user=Lakers |number=1579547850798948352 |title=The Lakers have signed guard Bryce Hamilton and requested waivers on guard LJ Figueroa.}} On October 22, 2022, Figueroa joined the [[South Bay Lakers]] training camp roster.{{cite web|url=https://lakersnation.com/south-bay-lakers-announce-2022-23-training-camp-roster-featuring-cole-swider-scotty-pippen-jr/2022/10/23/|website=lakersnation.com|title=South Bay Lakers Announce 2022-23 Training Camp Roster Featuring Cole Swider & Scotty Pippen Jr.|date=October 22, 2022|access-date=October 22, 2022}} ===Grises de Humacao (2023)=== On April 2, 2023, Figueroa signed with
